events.title: The death of Charlemagne
events.shortBlurb: The emperor crowned by the pope on Christmas Day, restorer of a Christian empire in the West, died at Aachen…
body: On 28 January 814 Charlemagne, king of the Franks and emperor of the Romans, died at Aachen and was buried the same day in the great church he had built there. Born in 747, he had ruled the Franks since 768, and on Christmas Day of 800 Pope Leo III had crowned him emperor in St. Peter's at Rome, reviving the imperial dignity in the West.

His wars made him lord of most of Western Christendom: he ended the Lombard kingdom in 774 and subdued the Saxons in a struggle of thirty years. A patron of letters, he gathered scholars such as Alcuin of York to his court, and the Carolingian revival of learning he fostered preserved the classical and Christian inheritance. His biographer Einhard left a vivid portrait of the man.

His only surviving son, Louis the Pious, succeeded him, but the empire did not long outlast his heirs: in 843 his grandsons divided it by the Treaty of Verdun. Yet the ideal he embodied, a Christian emperor ruling in alliance with the Church, governed the political imagination of Europe for a thousand years.
